findings.evidence: rgb(43, 108, 176) carries 6 unrelated meanings (badge-or-chip, border, bullet-or-dot, button, icon, text) across 34 marks — one color, one meaning (measured 6, threshold 3; composition-metrics.mjs). Context, not a re-derivation: in dark mode #2b6cb0 is the value of --emr-info (theme.css dark block), and it is also the middle stop of --emr-gradient-primary, which this round restored to the brand gradient in dark. The flagged marks are gradient and checked-state surfaces: the selected bilateral option, header tick bars, the selected drawing tool and size, R/L side chips, and the 34 selected waveform chips. The script ignores a severity colour only when it is byte-identical to a brand token. In dark, --emr-primary, --emr-secondary and --emr-accent are all #3182ce, so #2b6cb0 is no longer covered by that exception.
findings.recommendation: Fix this at the token level, not in components. Make dark mode follow the same pattern as light mode, where --emr-info equals --emr-accent (#3182ce). Either set dark --emr-info to #3182ce, or set dark --emr-secondary to #2b6cb0 so the gradient's middle stop is a declared brand value. Treat this as a palette decision for the token owner. With only four permitted blues, dark info and brand blues cannot be fully distinct, so you must pick which of them owns #2b6cb0.
